title: A receipt you tear off
summary: Pull the paper and watch the tear travel across: slow and clean, or quick and rough.

prompts.text:
Make a web page on a plain light-grey stage with a thin black pill-shaped printer slot and a white thermal receipt. Give the paper black monospace text, neat price columns, a small shop logo at the top (use a logo file if I give one), a small barcode and a fine zigzag bottom edge. Start with the already-printed receipt hidden behind the slot and slide the whole sheet down, bottom end first: the first visible print moves down with the paper and ends farthest from the slot. Never feed a blank sheet or add text line by line. Keep the whole receipt and a separate Reprint button visible, with no overlap even on a phone.

Let me grip either side of the paper with a mouse or finger. Make the tear feel like paper: it resists a little, then first splits at the corner closest to my grip and travels across the slot as I pull. Show that moving tear line before the paper comes free, even with a quick flick; if I pause partway, leave the remaining side attached. Keep a narrow paper stub in the slot. The stub and the torn piece must have opposite sides of the same cut, not two unrelated edges. A slow pull follows the cutter teeth, nearly straight with fine serrations. A quick pull takes an uneven path with tiny white paper fibres visible at the torn edge. As the last bit lets go, show a small visual snap, then let the torn paper curl, twist and fall with a soft shadow. No sound. Reprint clears the stub and feeds the next already-printed receipt the same way.

Build it with plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in a new folder inside the current project folder, open it in my browser when it is done, check in a browser that the feed and both tears work, and ask me before installing or loading anything.
prompts.label: A receipt that tears clean or jagged

action.label: Make a receipt you can tear
